title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calls for stronger regulation of AI: Exclusive
key_facts: Amodei gave an exclusive interview to ABC News.
He said Anthropic proposes stronger regulation, giving the government the ability, in a narrow way, to block deployment of unsafe technology.
His comments follow a letter on Wednesday saying the government should have power to block or deter deployment if third-party assessment finds unacceptable risks.
Alongside the essay he announced a $200 million investment in research on AI's impact on society.
On jobs he floated wage reinsurance, incentives against layoffs, better unemployment insurance and possible tax changes such as higher capital gains tax or taxes on AI companies.
On a pause he said all relevant players, including geopolitical adversaries, would have to agree and it would have to be verifiable.
He said China would not be a responsible actor with Mythos, Anthropic's model built to find software vulnerabilities, which was never widely released.
quote_evidence: We're proposing stronger regulation of the technology, proposing giving the government the ability, again, in a narrow way, to block deployment of unsafe technology.
It would have to be the case that all of the relevant AI players, including geopolitical adversaries, would have agree to it, and it would have be verifiable.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows a leading lab publicly asking for government power to stop an unsafe release.
notes: Interview date not stated; published 4 Oct.
